items.title: Route validate-channel git operations through the resolved gitRoot
items.context: validate-channel.ts:75-98 defaultGitLogReader and defaultGitChangedFilesReader run git rev-parse/merge-base/log/show with cwd: projectRoot (metadataRoot). Resolve authoritativeCwd via resolveStorySignedWorkspace() before checkCommitAuthor and pass it instead of projectRoot. Keep command text and pass/fail/skipped semantics unchanged.
items.userSees: With gitRoot configured to a subdirectory, `lattice validate --channel --story=B-xxx` runs the channel gate from the gitRoot and returns its normal pass/fail/skipped result instead of failing with 'fatal: not a git repository'.

happy.desc: wrapper-root fixture: inject gitLogReader + gitChangedFilesReader that capture cwd arg; call checkCommitAuthor with resolver returning authoritativeCwd=/repo/gitRoot -> both readers receive cwd=/repo/gitRoot, not /repo (metadataRoot); WHY: proves the reroute actually threads the resolved gitRoot into the git readers

plain-repo fixture: inject readers capturing cwd; call checkCommitAuthor with resolver returning resolved=false, authoritativeCwd=null -> both readers receive cwd=projectRoot (the original metadataRoot); WHY: proves null-fallback preserves byte-identical behavior for non-wrapper-root repos

wrapper-root fixture: run runChannelGateCli end-to-end with injected readers and resolver returning gitRoot -> gate returns pass/fail/skipped status matching the injected reader output, proving gate semantics unchanged; WHY: proves command text and pass/fail logic are not altered by the cwd reroute

edge.desc: resolver throws an exception during resolution -> handler catches and falls back to projectRoot rather than crashing the validate pipeline; WHY: protects against resolver bugs in production without blocking validation

wrapper-root with gitRoot pointing to a path that exists but is not the metadataRoot -> cwd is set to exactly the gitRoot path, not metadataRoot; WHY: ensures the reroute is not silently ignored when both paths exist

adversarial.desc: wrong-tree FALSE PASS guard: inject gitLogReader that returns data from the WRONG repo (metadataRoot commits instead of gitRoot commits) and assert the gate does NOT pass on stale/wrong data; WHY: a cwd mismatch could silently pass a gate by reading the wrong commit history

concurrent resolver: two validate-channel calls race with different storyIds returning different gitRoots -> each call uses its own resolved gitRoot, no cross-contamination; WHY: if resolver result is cached globally, a stale gitRoot from story A could bleed into story B validation

items.title: Route validate-concept git diff and grep scan through the resolved gitRoot
items.context: validate-concept.ts:78-91 defaultGitDiffReader (git diff base...HEAD) and defaultGrepReader (grep -rnF .) run with cwd: projectRoot (metadataRoot). Resolve authoritativeCwd and pass it so both the diff and the repo-wide grep run from the gitRoot. Keep IGNORED_DIRS / residual threshold logic unchanged.
items.userSees: With gitRoot configured to a subdirectory, `lattice validate --concept` computes deleted symbols and residual references against the gitRoot and reports residuals normally instead of failing with 'fatal: not a git repository'.

happy.desc: wrapper-root fixture: inject gitDiffReader + grepReader capturing cwd arg; call runConceptGateCli with resolver returning authoritativeCwd=/repo/gitRoot -> gitDiffReader receives cwd=/repo/gitRoot and grepReader receives cwd=/repo/gitRoot; WHY: proves both git diff and repo-wide grep are rerouted to the resolved gitRoot

plain-repo fixture: inject readers capturing cwd; runConceptGateCli with resolver returning resolved=false -> both readers receive cwd=projectRoot; WHY: proves null-fallback preserves byte-identical behavior on plain repos

end-to-end concept gate with injected diff containing deleted symbols: diff has -export function foo removed, grep finds 0 residuals -> status=pass, deletedSymbols=[foo], residuals=[]; WHY: proves IGNORED_DIRS and threshold logic unchanged after cwd reroute

edge.desc: gitDiffReader returns empty diff (no changes on branch) -> concept gate returns pass with deletedSymbols=[] regardless of wrapper-root vs plain-repo; WHY: empty-diff edge case should not crash or produce spurious residuals

grepReader called with a symbol containing special characters (underscore, dollar) in wrapper-root -> grep runs with -F (fixed string) from gitRoot, not metadataRoot; WHY: ensures -F flag and cwd are both correct when symbol has regex-special chars

adversarial.desc: wrong-tree FALSE PASS: inject grepReader that searches metadataRoot (wrong tree) instead of gitRoot and finds 0 residuals for a symbol that HAS residuals in the gitRoot -> assert concept gate must not pass with 0 residuals when the real tree has references; WHY: running grep from wrong cwd silently hides real residuals

maxBuffer exhaustion: inject gitDiffReader returning 50MB diff from gitRoot -> handler does not crash with ENOBUFS; WHY: large monorepo diffs from the correct gitRoot must not cause silent truncation that hides deleted symbols

items.title: Route cluster-sync commit scan through the resolved gitRoot
items.context: cluster-sync.ts:137-150 readCommitsSinceMain(projectRoot) runs git log main..HEAD with cwd: projectRoot (metadataRoot). Resolve authoritativeCwd and pass it instead so Resolves: CL-xxx commit scanning works under wrapper-root. Preserve the existing error-surfaced-as-warning behavior (F-023 path).
items.userSees: With gitRoot configured to a subdirectory, `lattice validate` auto-resolves Resolves: CL-xxx clusters from main..HEAD commits (or prints the git error as a warning) instead of silently finding no commits because git ran from the wrong root.

happy.desc: wrapper-root fixture: call readCommitsSinceMain with projectRoot=resolved gitRoot (/repo/gitRoot) -> execSync git log runs with cwd=/repo/gitRoot and returns parsed commits; WHY: proves the reroute threads the resolved gitRoot into the git log call site

plain-repo fixture: call readCommitsSinceMain with projectRoot=metadataRoot (resolver unresolved) -> cwd=projectRoot, commits returned byte-identical to pre-change behavior; WHY: proves null-fallback preserves existing behavior for non-wrapper-root repos

end-to-end syncClusterResolves with wrapper-root: commits contain Resolves: CL-001 -> cluster is resolved; WHY: proves the full pipeline from git log through commit parsing to cluster resolution works with the rerouted cwd

edge.desc: F-023 error path: readCommitsSinceMain from gitRoot where git log fails (no main branch) -> returns {commits:[], error: stderr_message} and syncClusterResolves surfaces the error as a warning, not a crash; WHY: preserves the F-023 error-surfaced-as-warning behavior after reroute
empty commit history: gitRoot has no commits on branch (main..HEAD is empty) -> returns {commits:[]} with no error; WHY: edge case where branch was just created with no divergence from main

adversarial.desc: wrong-tree FALSE PASS: readCommitsSinceMain called with metadataRoot (wrong tree) finds 0 commits because metadataRoot has no git history, while gitRoot has real commits with Resolves: CL-xxx -> assert syncClusterResolves must not silently report 0 resolved clusters when the real tree has matching commits; WHY: running git log from wrong cwd silently drops all cluster resolutions

commit message with malicious NUL/RS bytes: git log output contains extra \x00 and \x1e delimiters embedded in commit messages -> parser does not produce phantom commits or skip real ones; WHY: commit messages from the correct gitRoot could contain delimiter bytes that break the parser

items.title: Route worktree story_discard and story_advance merge git invocations through the resolved gitRoot
items.context: worktree.ts git()/gitFile() default cwd to root (metadataRoot); story_discard (:1049 status --porcelain, :1164 branch -D), story_advance merge (:958 rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD, :969 merge --no-ff), worktreeRemoveWithRetry (:258-259) and branchExists (:373-376) inherit it. Resolve authoritativeCwd and pass the resolved root explicitly to these git calls. Keep merge/discard control flow and Windows remove-retry unchanged. NOTE: worktree.ts:316 git add is NOT in scope (it already uses repoRoot; its missing -f flag is Bug 3).
items.userSees: With gitRoot configured to a subdirectory, `lattice story_discard` and `lattice story_advance --phase=DONE` (merge + branch cleanup) run git from the gitRoot and complete normally instead of aborting with 'fatal: not a git repository'.

happy.desc: wrapper-root fixture: call story_discard with resolver returning authoritativeCwd=/repo/gitRoot -> git status --porcelain, worktreeRemoveWithRetry, branchExists, and branch -D all run with cwd=/repo/gitRoot (not root=metadataRoot); assert by capturing cwd from injected git/execFileSync; WHY: proves all 5+ git call sites in discard path are rerouted

wrapper-root fixture: call story_advance --phase=DONE merge path with resolver returning authoritativeCwd=/repo/gitRoot -> git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD and git merge --no-ff run with cwd=/repo/gitRoot; WHY: proves merge-path git sites are rerouted

plain-repo fixture: call story_discard with resolver returning resolved=false -> all git calls use root (the original metadataRoot); WHY: proves null-fallback preserves byte-identical behavior for non-wrapper-root repos

edge.desc: worktreeRemoveWithRetry retry path: first 2 attempts fail with Permission denied from gitRoot, 3rd succeeds -> worktree removed, no crash; WHY: Windows retry logic must use the correct cwd on every retry attempt, not just the first

branchExists called after worktree removal with gitRoot -> git rev-parse runs from gitRoot to verify branch deletion; WHY: if branchExists falls back to metadataRoot after worktree removal it could report stale data

git add at worktree.ts:316 is NOT rerouted (out of scope, uses repoRoot) -> assert that line 316 cwd is still repoRoot, not gitRoot; WHY: scope boundary: this site is Bug 3, must not be accidentally changed

adversarial.desc: wrong-tree FALSE PASS on discard: git status --porcelain runs from metadataRoot (wrong tree) and reports clean, but gitRoot worktree has uncommitted changes -> assert story_discard must not proceed to delete the branch when the real worktree is dirty; WHY: a cwd mismatch silently discards uncommitted work

merge from wrong tree: git merge --no-ff runs from metadataRoot (no git repo) instead of gitRoot -> assert the merge must fail or be blocked, not silently succeed against the wrong repo; WHY: merging from the wrong cwd could merge unrelated branches or fail silently

items.title: Define and test the unresolved-gitRoot fallback for the rerouted git operations
items.context: resolveStorySignedWorkspace() can return resolved=false with authoritativeCwd=null (metadataRoot not git-backed, no worktree/gitRoot configured). Each rerouted site must fall back to the current projectRoot/root so non-wrapper-root repos stay byte-identical. Add tests via the readers' existing dependency-injection seams (do not spawn real git where injection exists): a wrapper-root fixture (metadataRoot != gitRoot) proving each site runs from gitRoot, and a plain-repo fixture proving unchanged behavior.
items.userSees: `lattice validate --story=B-xxx --json` on a plain (non-wrapper-root) repo produces the same channel/concept/cluster results as before this change, and the new wrapper-root test fixture passes, proving git ran from the gitRoot.

happy.desc: resolveGitCwd helper: pass storyCtx with resolver returning {resolved:true, authoritativeCwd:/repo/gitRoot} -> resolveGitCwd returns /repo/gitRoot; WHY: proves the helper extracts and returns the resolved authoritativeCwd

resolveGitCwd helper null-fallback: pass storyCtx with resolver returning {resolved:false, authoritativeCwd:null} -> resolveGitCwd returns projectRoot; WHY: proves the fallback to projectRoot when gitRoot is not configured

wrapper-root smoke test fixture: set up metadataRoot that is NOT a git repo + gitRoot subdir that IS a git repo; run all rerouted operations (validate-channel readers, validate-concept readers, readCommitsSinceMain, worktree git helpers) -> every git operation runs with cwd=gitRoot and succeeds (no fatal: not a git repository); WHY: integration test proving all ~14 sites are rerouted

plain-repo smoke test fixture: set up repo where metadataRoot IS a git repo, no gitRoot configured; run all rerouted operations -> every git operation runs with cwd=metadataRoot (projectRoot) and produces byte-identical results to pre-change behavior; WHY: regression guard for the majority of users who do not use wrapper-root

edge.desc: resolveGitCwd with authoritativeCwd set but resolved=false -> returns projectRoot (fallback), not the authoritativeCwd; WHY: resolved=false means the resolution is unreliable even if authoritativeCwd is non-null

all ~14 git call sites are covered by the smoke test: grep the modified source files for cwd: or execFileSync git or execSync git -> every site appears in the test coverage list; WHY: partial coverage is a regression risk — all sites must be tested
resolveGitCwd called with no storyId (e.g., during global validate) -> falls back to projectRoot without throwing; WHY: some validate paths may not have a story context

adversarial.desc: wrong-tree FALSE PASS comprehensive: wrapper-root fixture where metadataRoot accidentally has a .git dir (stale/leftover) AND gitRoot has the real repo -> assert all operations use gitRoot not metadataRoot, even though metadataRoot would succeed as a git command target; WHY: if the fallback triggers incorrectly when both dirs have .git, gates could pass against the wrong commit history

no git command text changed: diff the modified files and assert that no git command string (the arguments to git log/diff/grep/merge/branch/rev-parse/show/status) is altered — only the cwd parameter changes; WHY: scope constraint is cwd-only, any command text change is a scope violation

no gate semantics changed: run the same validate scenario before and after the change on a plain repo -> JSON output is byte-identical (same pass/fail/skipped, same offenders, same residuals); WHY: the fix must be transparent to gate consumers

function signatures back-compatible: checkCommitAuthor, runConceptGateCli, readCommitsSinceMain, syncClusterResolves, git(), gitFile(), branchExists() -> all accept their pre-change parameter signatures (no required new params that break callers); build must pass; WHY: signature breakage would fail downstream callers
